title: model loading breadcrumbs - weights shard failures (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
- Investigating recurring model load failures for a handful of customer uploads (mostly GPTQ-style sharded weights). Failures appear during the final assembly step after download. Customer reported increased incidents after switching to multipart upload pipeline (uploader service v2).

Symptoms observed (incidents):
- Instance logs show loader failing with different errors across runs:
  - "ValueError: Unexpected EOF while reading weights" (python loader, safetensors backend)
  - "Checksum mismatch: expected 3f2c8a..., got 9b1a7d..." (post-download verify step)
  - "RuntimeError: missing tensor 'transformer.wte.weight' in checkpoint" (assembly/concat step)
  - "IndexError: shard index out of range while mapping shards -> tensors" (sharded manifest parsing)
- Failures intermittent: same model sometimes loads fine after retrying or after re-downloading shards manually.
- Failed loads correlate with uploader v2 rollouts (INF-3421) and a spike in partial put-object artifacts on S3.

Commands / repro steps I ran locally (notes + outputs):
1) Reproduce download + verify from S3 (linux box):
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/gptq/v1/model-abc/shard-000.safetensors /tmp/model/ --no-progress 2>&1 | tee /tmp/cp-shard-000.log
   md5sum /tmp/model/shard-000.safetensors -> 9b1a7d3f...
   (manifest expected md5 = 3f2c8a9d...)
   tail -n 50 /tmp/cp-shard-000.log:
   -> Completed 256 MiB/256 MiB in 00:03
   -> No obvious network error.

2) Pipeline loader run (docker image: redwood/loader:main)
   docker run --rm -v /tmp/model:/data redwood/loader:main load --manifest /data/manifest.json --out /data/assembled.pt 2>&1 | tee /tmp/loader.log
   Partial logs:
   2026-02-26 11:32:43,112 INFO reading manifest /data/manifest.json
   2026-02-26 11:32:44,220 ERROR shard /data/shard-000.safetensors checksum mismatch (expected 3f2c8a9d, got 9b1a7d3f)
   2026-02-26 11:32:44,221 ERROR aborting assembly due to shard integrity failure

3) Attempted manual concat (python quick script) -> fails with Unexpected EOF:
   python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; f=safe_open('/tmp/model/shard-000.safetensors','rb')
   -> ValueError: Unexpected EOF while reading header

4) Tried copying from GCS mirror (rclone):
   rclone copy remote:redwood-models/gptq/v1/model-abc /tmp/model -P --s3-server-side-encryption=AES256
   -> rclone reported success, but md5 still mismatched.

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
- Hypothesis A: Uploads occasionally leave truncated objects (uploader v2 race/stream flush bug) -> result is full size object on S3 but truncated content at tail (header/footer inconsistent). Checksums in manifest reflect pre-upload digest. Explains checksum mismatch + EOF.
- Hypothesis B: Manifest generation (uploader) is sometimes computed from local shards before final multipart reassembly completes -> manifest contains digest of ephemeral file; a later multipart commit changed the object boundary, mismatch results.
- Hypothesis C: Sharder tool produced mixed formats (some shards gzipped), loader doesn't detect gzip header -> EOF/parse errors.
- Hypothesis D: Network caching/proxy manipulated content (less likely given local direct cp reproduces mismatch).
- Hypothesis E: Transient s3 eventual-consistency edge case where MD5 reported by API differs until object fully propagated (unlikely for us, S3 provides strong read-after-write for new objects).

Debugging steps already tried (and results):
- Re-downloaded multiple times from different regions -> still inconsistent md5 on same model for some shards.
- Compared object size via aws s3api head-object -> sizes match expected size in manifest but content checks fail (suggests content truncated but header size set?).
- Ran aws s3api get-object --range to fetch last 1KB of object -> for bad shards, last bytes are zeros or repeated patterns instead of expected safetensors footer.
- Pulled CloudTrail events for PutObject/CompleteMultipartUpload around the timestamps -> found some multipart uploads completed by uploader service with unusually short commit-time differences (CompleteMultipartUpload immediately after last part upload).
- Replayed uploader v1 path for same model -> produced shards with correct checksums and loader succeeded.

Immediate mitigations & workarounds applied:
- Added download-time checksum validation to loader, with automatic retry and exponential backoff (currently in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1234).
- Added a post-download verify step that fails fast and triggers an auto-requeue of model load (so customers don't get flaky runtime errors).
- For critical customers, asked infra to re-upload affected model artifacts using uploader v1 path (manual, stopgap).

Longer-term fixes to investigate / next steps:
1) Root cause capture: instrument uploader v2 to emit upload-part checksums and CompleteMultipartUpload latency; correlate with bad manifests (INF-3421).
2) Add server-side manifest versioning + artifact atomicity markers: writer should write manifest only after all part commits confirmed. Loader should reject manifest older than commit-time marker.
3) Improve uploader unit tests for multipart commit ordering and simulated network interruptions.
4) Add a lightweight per-shard safetensors header validator to uploader and CI (detect gzipped shards, truncated writes).
5) Consider switching customer-facing manifest format to include per-shard length + sha256 (not just md5) and a manifest signature to prevent partial/early-manifest publication.
6) Improve loader error messages to surface whether mismatch is size vs digest vs EOF to help quicker triage.

Notes / things to ask infra / uploader team:
- Can we get logs for multipart uploads for model-abc between 2026-02-20 and 2026-02-24? (timestamps in incident tickets)
- Any recent changes to the streaming flush / fsync code in uploader v2? (PRs around Jan-Feb 2026)
- Are there cases where CompleteMultipartUpload is invoked while last part is still processing (bug in async ack)?

Quick checklist for me (manual steps):
- [x] re-download shards and capture md5 + tail bytes
- [x] run safetensors header check on each shard (script saved at ~/scripts/check_safetensors.sh)
- [x] escalate to uploader team with copies of bad shards attached (s3 presigned links)
- [ ] instrument loader to log full shard object ETag + Content-Length during download attempts
- [ ] add small integration test to CI that uploads/downloads a 256MB shard via uploader v2 and verifies digest on the other end

Raw error snippets (copied from logs):
- 2026-02-26T11:32:44.220Z ERROR shard /data/shard-000.safetensors checksum mismatch (expected=3f2c8a9d, actual=9b1a7d3f)
- Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/opt/loader/loader.py", line 412, in assemble_shards
      with safe_open(shard_fp, 'rb') as f:
    File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/safetensors/__init__.py", line 98, in safe_open
      raise ValueError("Unexpected EOF while reading header")
  ValueError: Unexpected EOF while reading header
- 2026-02-27T03:14:12Z ERROR failed to map shards: IndexError('list index out of range') manifest parsing failed (shard count 8, found files 7)

Attachments / artifacts I left for follow-up:
- s3://redwood-models/gptq/v1/model-abc/ (presigned links in ticket INF-3421)
- local collected bad shard samples: /tmp/bad-shards/model-abc/* (sha256 list attached to ticket)
- quick validation script: ~/scripts/check_safetensors.sh (bash script, uses head + tail + python safetensors header check)

Bottom line: high-priority intermittent corruption during upload/commit path. Immediate detection + retry reduces customer impact; root cause likely in uploader v2 multipart commit ordering or flush. Next step is to get uploader multipart timelines and add stricter atomicity guarantees to uploader and manifest publication.

Timestamped notes (working):
- 2026-02-25 09:14: created initial repro and collected first bad shard
- 2026-02-26 11:40: asked infra for multipart logs (ticket INF-3421)
- 2026-02-27 16:05: implemented loader-level retry + checksum validation (wip PR)
- 2026-03-03 14:20: got confirmation uploader team will repro locally and add extra fsyncs

Signed-off: Lexi (quick scratchpad, will formalize into incident report once uploader team confirms root cause)
